title: Austin's Future: Fire, Parks, and a New Arena
summary:
*   **Bond Election Scheduled:** City leaders initiated an election for new bonds to fund significant city-wide upgrades and improvements.
*   **Public Safety & Infrastructure Boost:** Proposals included four new fire stations (with one specifically for the Montopolis area), expanding the police and courts building, extensive street paving, and drainage improvements, including allocations for East Austin.
*   **Community & Recreation Enhancements:** Plans featured new mobile health units, neighborhood playgrounds, a new library in the 10th Ward, and major park developments like a new golf course at Decker Lake.
*   **Major $14 Million Convention Center/Sports Arena:** A substantial project was proposed for a new convention center and sports arena, highlighted for its potential to create employment opportunities, particularly in East Austin.

Mayor LaRue stated that this was a called Special Meeting for the purpose of calling an
election to authorize the issuance of revenue-supported bonds and general obligation bonds
of the City of Austin, and taking such action as necessary in connection therewith.
Mr. Guerrero, representing the East First Neighborhood Center, directed a series of
questions to the Council covering various items in the bond issue.
Those items were included in the following: Health Department Two mobile health units were
proposed out of CIP funds, not bond funds, at $25,000 each, to be used City-wide, both day
and night. Larger units would be purchased than the existing unit. The funding did not
include staff. Hospital A standby generator was proposed at about $50,000 for emergency
use at the hospital. There was some discussion regarding the new hospital and staffing of
it. Fire Department Four new stations were proposed: southeast Austin (Montopolis area),
southwest, northwest and generally north. There was no fire station in Montopolis at
present, but was served by the Airport fire station. Each station cost about $200,000 to
build, plus some equipment, and cost $100,000 annually to operate. مالد

Police and Courts
Expansion of the existing police and courts building was planned to give the Police
Department adequate space and to speed up the trial process. Public Works Mr. Reuben
Rountree listed the streets to be paved in East Austin under the bond issue and through
the voluntary paving program. Sidewalks The City Manager was recommending to the Council
that a flat fee, such as $1.00 or $1.25 per foot, be charged for sidewalks so that the
owner would know in advance what the charge would be. The City would pay the difference.
Railroad Crossing Ten to twelve railroad crossings were already scheduled and others were
scheduled within the next five years. on Interregional Highway near Hancock Center.
Drainage Plans had already been drawn for the crossing Existing drainage way improvements
under the bond issue in the Capital Improvements Program totaled $190,000 with $40,000
being spent in East Austin.
$25,000 was proposed for the Montopolis area. Service Yards An East end service yard was
proposed at a cost of $800,000 to be built east of the City in the Townview area (about
175 acres). Two other facilities were planned, one to the north and one to the south of
the City. Parks and Recreation $200,000 would be spent for new neighborhood playgrounds,
to be built adjacent to new elementary schools. It was planned to open up six to eight new
ones within the next five years. $140,000 would be spent to rehabilitate existing
playgrounds, with $30,000 being spent in East Austin. Decker Lake $200,000 would be spent
on development of Decker Lake. It was anticipated that some funds would be coming from the
private sector to develop the lake area further.

10 Major Park Additions
$500,000 was proposed to build an additional golf course, to be located at Decker Lake.
The new course would take some of the load off the Morris Williams Course.
Indoor-Outdoor Pool or Tennis Center
Only one of the items, possibly the covering of Ramsey Pool would be done at this time.
$5,000 was budgeted for the item. Softball Mr. Beverly Sheffield stated that a softball
field complex was being considered for the Walnut Creek area which would include at least
four diamonds. Library A library facility for the 10th Ward area was proposed at a cost of
$100,000.
The facility would be an outlet for books and a place where the bookmobiles could come to
pick up books to service the surrounding areas. Convention Center/Sports Arena Up to $14
million was proposed for a convention center/sports arena, which would provide employment
for more members of the East Austin community. The Municipal Auditorium would still be
used for smaller conventions and meetings. Park Site Mr. Gutierrez asked about a park
which was supposed to be built in the Meadowbrook Rehabilitation Project. The City Manager
stated that the City was trying to find a better location in the area for the park because
the proposed location was not very accessible. An 11-acre City-owned tract at Cumberland
and South Fifth was being considered as a park site. There were no plans to extend Gillis
Park.
Mrs. Janes H. Means, a member of the Parks and Recreation Board, spoke regarding Givens
Park located at East 12th Street down by Webberville Road and Oak Springs Drive. She was
concerned that the $175,000 budgeted for six parks would not be sufficient to build a
proposed multipurpose center at Givens Park.
Mr. Dick Brown addressed the Council to speak in favor of the total bond issue. Mr. C. T.
Uselton spoke in favor of the bond issue, including the convention center,
